references.text: The direct fulfillment of the Lord's command, where Moses makes a bronze snake and sets it on a pole.
Moses raises a banner (נֵס) as a sign of the Lord's intervention; the same Hebrew word is used for the pole.
Isaiah's shoot shall stand as a banner (נֵס) for the peoples, a messianic prophecy using the same imagery.
The Lord lifts His banner for the nations, the same Hebrew word (נֵס) as a symbol of salvation.
King Hezekiah breaks the bronze snake that Moses had made because the Israelites had begun to worship it.
Jesus refers directly to this event and compares Himself to the snake that was lifted up, so that everyone who believes may have eternal life.
